title: Annex 3A — Product Specific Rules of Origin
note: The rule a good must satisfy to be an originating good. Rules are read most-specific-first: sub-heading, then heading, then chapter. A Section Note, where one exists, sits above all of them.

glossary.WO: Wholly obtained. The good must be entirely obtained or produced in India — grown, mined, born and raised, or made exclusively from materials that themselves qualify. Article 3.3.
glossary.CC: Change of chapter. Every non-originating material must be classified in a different 2-digit HS chapter from the finished good.
glossary.CTH: Change of tariff heading. Every non-originating material must be classified in a different 4-digit HS heading from the finished good.
glossary.CTSH: Change of tariff sub-heading. Every non-originating material must be classified in a different 6-digit HS sub-heading from the finished good.
glossary.QVC: Qualifying value content. A stated percentage of the good's value must be accounted for by originating content, calculated under Article 3.5 by either the build-up or the build-down method.
glossary.Standard QVC: Standard qualifying value content: 40% of the ex-works price or 45% of the FOB value under the build-down method, or 35% of either under the build-up method. Article 3.5.

sectionNotes.title: VEGETABLE PRODUCTS
sectionNotes.note: Section Note: An agricultural or horticultural good grown in the territory of a Party is originating even if grown from seed, bulbs, rhizomes, rootstock, cuttings, slips, grafts, shoots, buds, or other live parts of plants that are imported from a non-Party.

sectionNotes.title: PRODUCTS OF THE CHEMICAL OR ALLIED INDUSTRIES
sectionNotes.note: Section Note 1: Chemical Reaction Rule Notwithstanding the applicable product specific rules of origin, a good of chapter 28 through 38 that is the product of a chemical reaction satisfies the requirements of this Annex if the chemical reaction occurs in the territory of one or both of the Parties. For the purposes of this rule: “chemical reaction” means a process (including a biochemical process) which results in a molecule with a new structure by breaking intramolecular bonds and by forming new intramolecular bonds, or by altering the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule. The following are not chemical reactions: (a) dissolving in water or other solvents; (b) the elimination of solvents including solvent water; or (c) the addition or elimination of water of crystallisation. Section Note 2: Mixing and Blending Rule Notwithstanding the applicable product specific rules of origin, a good of chapter 33, satisfies the requirements of this Annex if mixing and blending occurred in the territory of one or both of the Parties. For the purposes of this rule: “mixing and blending” means the deliberate and proportionally controlled mixing or blending (including dispersing) of materials other than the addition of diluents, to conform to predetermined specifications which results in the production of a good having physical or chemical characteristics which are relevant to the purposes or uses of the good and are different from the input materials.

sectionNotes.title: PLASTICS AND ARTICLES THEREOF; RUBBER AND ARTICLES THEREOF
sectionNotes.note: Section Note 1: Chemical Reaction Rule Notwithstanding the applicable product specific rules of origin, a good of chapter 39 that is the product of a chemical reaction satisfies the requirements of this Annex if the chemical reaction occurs in the territory of one or both of the Parties. For the purposes of this rule: “chemical reaction” means a process (including a biochemical process) which results in a molecule with a new structure by breaking intramolecular bonds and by forming new intramolecular bonds, or by altering the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule.
